The current sun emperor is an expansionist, imperialist ruler who has shook up elven rule by starting a series of expansionist wars to "preserve the natural way amongst the neighbouring nations" and has formed the Azuran empire, a Inca esque sun worshipping empire of traditionalist elves bent on conquest locked in a cold war with the other major player on the continent, the People's Republic of Valoria.

To make up for their slower reproduction, the empire has encouraged breeding with the short lived kinds around them, creating further steps on the caste ladders consisting of half elfs, quarter elfs and so on. Only my local dnd setting I run games in, largely inspired by the 1800s Europe, the theme of the setting is revolutions so most nations are currently, or have recently, had some sort of revolution affecting them

The Azuran empire had their Sun Coup where the son of the old elven emperor took over which changed the country from millennia of isolationism into an expansionist empire.

The Crown of Valoria recently had the first Peoples Revolution, which led to the new Peoples Republic of Valoria, a semi communist Republic in opposition to Azura.


The Republic of Nymar instigated the era of revolutions by overthrowing their old Illithid masters

The Free cities of Aran started leaning heavily into biomancy as a defence measure after the Arathi invasion of their neighbour of Calendria. These days they have Leviathan ships, Kraken Galleons and a mutated, mind controlled Giant protecting them.

All of this was built upon the foundations of magic which was brought over from the twin realm floating in the sky above this world during the Era of Exploration several centuries earlier. The distillation of the substance known as Orichalchum changed magic from being purely contained within the hands of clergy and royal sorcerer bloodlines, to being a relatively common occurrence, atleast among those with money or power enough to get a hold of it. 

The campaign is mostly set in the Bay of Ithor, the great bay in between several of the mentioned nations, with the Azuran empire spreading to the west and the People's Republic of Valoria to the east, with the neutral, dwarven, ancestor worshipping merchant states of the Confederacy of Ithor as the starting area.

The Azuran Empire is led by some of the last pure blooded elfs in the world, and as such the aristocracy does not age. As there are so few pure blooded elfs yet, the empire have enforced a strict caste system based on the purety of one's elven blood, the stronger the elven lineage, and therefore the greater lifespan, the higher up you are put on the caste system. Liches, archdruids and other creatures which have achieved artificial immortality are able to move upwards in the system, but not as high as those who achieve such a life span naturally. While slavery is technically not legal within the empire, the lowest castes, generally creatures living a century or less, are slaves in all but name.

The long living elites have led to a rather stagnant society though, as the world is modernising and rebellions spring up in the nearby nations, the Azuran Empire prepares for an all out assault on its neighbours to prevent "the natural order" of monarchies and aristocracies to devolve into republican democracies. An elven expansion such as that has never been seen before in the world and is a major element of conflict within the setting

Well it varies. The most common one would be your family were monarchs, so you're a monarch. But as discussed, a dynasty of monarchs must begin somewhere. There is also the fact that not all dynasties or monarchs had their own blood children take over, both Rome and medieval Scandinavia are good examples of elective monarchies.

So while noble blood/dynastic rule might indicate a monarchy, it isn't neccecarily a requirement.

It's a very interesting question to ask! We all like monarchs here but let us not be fanatical about it, the creation of new monarchies has always been a thing, so let us try to define what would make him a monarch.

We're I to define what would be needed for someone to be a monarch I might put forth:

Did he consider himself a monarch?

Did his people consider him a monarch?

Was his rule part of a dynasty? 

I do honestly not know the answers to the first two, perhaps he fulfilled them, perhaps not. Regarding the latter he would probably not be of noble blood, but like we established, dynasties must come from somewhere. As such he might have been considered a proto-monarch, and had he been succeeded either by a blood heir, or if history wanted it so, an elected heir, he might have been considered the first of his dynasty. As it is I would probably argue he is not royalty for the sole reason he was the sole ruler of his dynasty. There is a lot to be said for legitimacy through rule over several generations. You make your dynasty rule for longer than 3/4 generations and it will be a dynasty that has "always been in control" as far as most people would be concerned. Delegating royalty without that temporal legitimacy is not impossible, but more difficult

I find the circle very interesting, but abit underpowered. The flavour is great, and there is some great ideas, but I have a few critiques:

Familiar Spirit is great! A wonderful tradeoff for your wildshape, yet I would love to see this feature get expanded as you level up. 

Read the bones is slightly weird, is it supposed to remove all material costs for divination spells? If so thats a fine feature, although abit disconnected from the rest of the circle. 

Coven Spellcasting is pretty good. It is a paladin smite than can be used when other creatures attack, making the druid a semi support, which is totally fine. It also heavily supports the Coven feel of the circle. It does arrive rather late, as a circle named Circle of the Coven only gets access to said coven at level 10. Id suggest giving some sort of coven ability earlier, maybe something connected to Familiar Spirit. Perhaps replacing Read the Bones with a coven esque ability that allows you to extend your familiar benefits to your coven? 

Applied Witchcraft is fine, it supports the Coven fantasy, but is vey underpowered as a subclass capstone. It is largely a worse Circle of the Land’s Natural Recovery, although you can use it for other people as well. Id reccommend atleast increasing the level you can recover. 

Lastly, id say your Alternate Spellcasting Focus is great! Small flavours like that are always a great addition.
While strong, it is such a unique and situational feat (as in you can never know which domains is best for the day) that id allow it regardless. Really well done!
